name: LoyiCard
tagline: Digital stamp and points loyalty cards that live in Apple Wallet and Google Wallet, aimed at small shops and salons.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The actual logic here is trivial: customers, stamps, a redemption threshold, and a QR code the staff scans. An agent can produce that plus a staff scanning screen and a customer web card in a single session. The part that bites is the wallet integration: Apple Wallet passes need a paid Apple Developer account and a Pass Type ID certificate, and push updates to a pass that is already issued need a pass web service plus APNs. Google Wallet wants an issuer account and service account keys. So the DIY version is real and useful, it just starts life as a mobile web page with a QR code instead of a pass that sits next to your boarding passes.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where staff scan a customer QR to add a stamp, customers open a phone-friendly card page showing their progress, and reaching the threshold flags a reward to redeem.
requirements: Node and a machine or small VPS to host it
A domain or tunnel so customer card links work on phones
Apple Developer account plus Pass Type ID certificate if you want real Apple Wallet passes
Google Wallet issuer account and service account key for Android passes
Push notifications or SMS need a separate provider and are out of scope by default
whatYouLose: Signed Apple and Google Wallet passes out of the box, including automatic updates to a pass the customer already added
Push notifications to wallet passes, which is the main reason businesses buy this category
A polished card designer with logos, colours and templates that non technical owners can use
Multi location staff accounts, roles and anti fraud checks on stamp scanning
Someone else keeping the pass certificates renewed and the Apple and Google APIs working when they change
moatNotes: The moat is a certificate chain and two platform relationships, not the loyalty math.
whyPeopleStillPay: A barbershop owner is not going to maintain an Apple Pass Type ID certificate, a pass web service and an APNs connection so that a stamp card updates silently on a customer's lock screen. That plumbing is the whole product, and it is the part that quietly breaks. Paying a small monthly fee to never think about it again is a rational trade for anyone whose actual job is cutting hair.
notes: Build the web card version first and see if your customers even care about wallet passes; plenty of shops find a bookmarked link is enough.
prompt:
Build a self hosted digital loyalty card system in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions: Node 20, TypeScript, Fastify, SQLite via better-sqlite3, server rendered HTML with Eta templates, plain CSS, no frontend framework, no build step beyond tsc.

Data model:
- business: name, logo url, stamps_required, reward_text
- customer: id (uuid), name optional, phone optional, created_at, token (random 24 char url safe string)
- stamp: id, customer_id, created_at, staff_note optional
- redemption: id, customer_id, created_at

Routes:
- GET /c/:token : public customer card page, mobile first, shows business name, filled and empty stamp icons, progress text, the reward, and a large QR code encoding the absolute URL https://HOST/staff/scan/:token
- GET /staff : passphrase gated (STAFF_PASSPHRASE in .env, signed cookie session), shows a customer list and an "add customer" form that returns the new card link and a printable QR
- GET /staff/scan/:token : shows the customer, current stamp count, an "add stamp" button and, when the count is at or above stamps_required, a "redeem reward" button
- POST /staff/stamp/:token and POST /staff/redeem/:token : write rows, redeem resets the counter by recording a redemption and only counting stamps created after the last redemption
- GET /admin/settings : edit business name, stamps_required, reward_text

Rules:
- Reject a second stamp for the same customer within a configurable cooldown (default 60 seconds) to stop double scans, show a clear message
- Seed the database on first run with the business row and three demo customers
- Secrets only in .env, with .env.example committed
- No analytics, no telemetry, no external accounts, no email or SMS
- Apple Wallet and Google Wallet passes are explicitly out of scope: instead print a clear README section explaining exactly what a real .pkpass would require (Apple Developer account, Pass Type ID certificate, pass web service, APNs) and leave a src/wallet/README.md stub describing where that code would plug in
- Include a README with setup, a single npm run dev command, and instructions for exposing the server over a tunnel so phone links work
